cover.headline: A cash-rich subsidiary of a Japanese major, priced for growth it has not delivered
cover.lead: Sumitomo Chemical India sells crop-protection chemicals to Indian farmers through 40,000 dealers: about 71% generic products inherited from Excel Crop Care, and 29% patented molecules from its 75% parent, Sumitomo Chemical of Japan. It has no debt and ₹2,523 cr of cash. But revenue has not grown since FY23, domestic sales fell 3% in Q1FY27, and the June-September monsoon ended 12.6% below normal, the weakest since 2015. The street values it on **P/E on FY28E earnings (36-45x)**, with 13-21% a year of earnings growth; we forecast ~10%. Applying **28x to Sep-28E EPS of ₹13.7** gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with SELL.** The cross-checks are lower still (EV/EBITDA ₹357, DCF ₹249) because a P/E on total profit capitalises the interest on the cash pile at 28x. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: Growth has stalled for three years
arguments.p: Revenue was ₹3,511 cr in FY23 and ₹3,238 cr in FY26; domestic crop-protection sales were lower in FY26 than in FY23 (standalone ₹2,485 cr vs ₹2,607 cr). Management concedes peers have grown faster. Q1FY27 revenue rose 1%, with domestic sales down 3%.

arguments.h: The parent is both the moat and the ceiling
arguments.p: Exclusive Indian rights to Sumitomo Japan's patented molecules give the company its best products (Excalia Max and Lentigo, launched in FY26). But the parent decides the timing: it dropped and then restored the animal-nutrition business, it has started charging a royalty, sales to Japan fell in Q1, and its new semiconductor-materials pact in India (with Tata Electronics, 19-Sep-2026) was signed by the parent, not the listed company.

₹2,523 cr of cash (Jun-2026), ~12% of the market value, earns ~7% before tax; the payout is ~12% and there has been no buyback. The core business earns ~35% on its own equity; the cash drags group ROE down to 16-17%.

The stock is 23% below its 52-week high of ₹565 and trades at 36.1x our FY27E earnings, versus a ~42x forward median since 2023. On the street's method, our lower growth and the sector's de-rating, 28x gives {{dcf.upside|chg}}, and the cash-adjusted cross-checks give less.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (late Oct-2026): how much the deficient monsoon cut the kharif season.
IMD's first monsoon forecast for 2027 (April): the FY28 recovery depends on it.
Delhi High Court on the glyphosate restriction (~11-15% of revenue); paraquat's final ban (22-Sep-2026) is an opportunity.
Parent decisions: exports to Japan, new molecules for India, and whether its semiconductor-materials plans involve the listed company.
Bhavnagar plant for the parent (Q4FY27); any use of the cash (acquisition or payout).

sections.title: Two businesses under one roof: Excel's generics and Sumitomo's patents

blocks.p: Sumitomo Chemical India (SCIL) is the Indian arm of Sumitomo Chemical, Japan's eighth-largest crop-protection company globally. It was a small distributor of its parent's products until 2016-19, when it bought and merged Excel Crop Care, a listed Indian maker of generic pesticides with its own plants and brands. Today it does two quite different things: it **makes and sells generic products** (glyphosate, chlorpyriphos, profenofos, aluminium phosphide) that compete on price with Indian and Chinese makers (~71% of revenue); and it **sells the parent's patented molecules** under Sumitomo brands (~29%), often formulating them locally. It also exports, distributes household insecticides, and passes through animal-feed additives (methionine) for the parent at a fixed 4-5% margin.

sections.title: A ₹31,000 cr market growing 5-6% a year, ruled by the monsoon

blocks.p: India's domestic crop-protection market was about ₹30,800 cr in FY25 and is expected to grow 5-6% a year to FY28 (CRISIL). Indian farmers use far less than most countries (~0.6 kg per hectare vs ~3 kg in the US and ~12.6 kg in Brazil), so there is long-term room, but demand in any one year depends on the monsoon, pest attacks and crop prices. India is also the world's third-largest exporter of these chemicals (~₹38,000 cr in FY25), mainly generics, priced against Chinese supply. The market is fragmented: global innovators (Bayer, Syngenta, BASF, Corteva, Sumitomo), large Indian firms (UPL, PI, Coromandel, Rallis, Dhanuka) and hundreds of small generic makers.

sections.title: The parent: the source of the best products, and of the biggest uncertainty

blocks.p: Sumitomo Chemical (SCC) owns 75% and supplies the molecules that set SCIL apart from Indian generic makers. SCIL has the exclusive right to sell SCC's patented products in India under SCC brands, historically without paying a royalty. India has recently been moved into SCC's first tier of countries for early trials of new molecules (two are in Indian trials before their global launch). SCC also wants India as a manufacturing base: SCIL is building plants at Bhavnagar, Tarapur and Dahej to make molecules for SCC worldwide.

blocks.title: Moat scorecard
blocks.source: GAM research compilation (company filings and calls to Sep-2026)

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** SCIL has a **distribution moat** (one of the widest dealer networks in Indian agrochemicals, with disciplined credit: receivables 83 days and almost no sales returns) and **privileged access to a global innovator's molecules**. That explains its ~20% EBITDA margin, above Indian generic peers. But it has **no cost advantage** in the 71% of revenue that is generic, and **no research of its own** (0.45% of sales). A distribution business with a borrowed pipeline deserves a premium to generic makers, but not the 40x+ that assumes it can grow at mid-teens: it has not done so since FY23.

sections.title: A monsoon business: two quarters make two-thirds of the profit

blocks.p: Most of India's crops are sown in the kharif (monsoon) season from June to September, and that is when farmers spray most insecticides and herbicides. So April-September (Q1 and Q2) is Sumitomo's peak: in FY26 the first half brought 61% of revenue and 66% of net profit. October-March (rabi, the winter crop) is smaller. One weak monsoon, or one season of excess stock at dealers, can wipe out a year's growth.

pair.title: Quarterly revenue: peaks every June and September quarter
Quarterly net profit

blocks.callout: **The current season is weak:** Q1FY27 revenue rose only 1% (domestic −3%) as the monsoon arrived late, and the June-September monsoon ended about 13% below normal, the weakest since 2015. Q1 net profit rose 20%, but mainly because other income almost doubled, partly from a one-off ₹27 cr insurance claim for a 2023 plant fire. This matters for valuation: the June and September quarters set the tone for the whole year.

sections.title: Revenue has stalled for three years; profit grew on margins and interest income

blocks.p: Sumitomo Chemical India's revenue rose from ₹2,425 cr in FY20 to ₹3,511 cr in FY23, then fell 19% in FY24 as the whole Indian crop-protection industry cut prices and cleared excess stock. It has recovered only to ₹3,238 cr in FY26, so revenue is still 8% below its FY23 peak. Profit has done better: net profit reached a record ₹543 cr in FY26 because the EBITDA margin rose to 20.7% (from 13.8% in FY20) and interest income on a growing cash pile added ₹131 cr.

pair.title: Revenue: flat since FY23
Net profit: a record ₹543 cr in FY26
EBITDA margin: up from 14% to 21%
Other income now ~18% of pre-tax profit

blocks.callout: **Our view:** over FY23-26 revenue fell 3% a year while net profit grew 3% a year. The gap came from a higher margin and treasury income. Both have limits: the margin is already at a record, and interest income grows only as fast as the cash pile. Profit growth from here needs revenue growth.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit, but watch interest income, dealer schemes and one-offs

bullets: **Interest income.** Other income was ₹147 cr in FY26, ~20% of pre-tax profit. It grows only as fast as the cash pile and falls when deposit rates fall; it should not be valued like operating profit.

**Dealer rebates and schemes.** Revenue is shown after ₹333 cr of rebates and discounts (9.3% of gross sales). The auditor flags the estimate as a key audit matter. The year-end liability for "additional discounts and schemes" rose 16.5% in FY26 while sales rose 3%.
**Sales returns** were ₹22 cr in FY26 (₹9 cr in FY25) but remain tiny (0.6% of gross sales); management says it has no sales-return policy.
**One-offs.** Q1FY27 profit included a ₹27 cr insurance claim for a 2023 fire at Bhavnagar; Q3FY26 included a ₹16 cr Labour Codes charge.
**Animal-nutrition pass-through** sales (₹185 cr in FY26, up to ₹1,000 cr of purchases approved for FY27) add revenue at a 4-5% margin: they flatter growth and dilute the margin percentage.
**Barrix goodwill** of ₹60 cr sits on a business that made ₹0.08 cr profit in FY26 (impairment test is a key audit matter).
**Data note.** Screener shows an 80% payout for FY25; it belongs to FY24 (₹5 special dividend). FY25's payout was ~12%.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** The audit (B S R & Co., KPMG network, since FY25) is unqualified and the business generates real cash (₹446 cr operating cash flow in FY26). The amber is for the growing dealer-scheme liability and the large share of profit that comes from interest income.

sections.title: No debt, a growing cash pile, and dealer credit as the main use of money

blocks.p: Sumitomo carries almost no debt (₹63 cr, mostly leases). Over FY21-26 it generated ₹2,691 cr of operating cash, spent only ₹414 cr on capex and paid ₹532 cr in dividends (including a ₹5 special dividend in FY24), so cash has piled up: ₹2,113 cr at Mar-2026 and ₹2,549 cr at Jun-2026 on the company's own count, which includes ~₹840 cr of deposits placed with companies and banks that sit under "other assets" in the balance sheet below. The main use of working capital is credit to dealers and stock for the season: receivable days have fallen from 128 in FY20 to 83 in FY26, while inventory days (166) remain high, as is normal in crop protection, where products must be stocked months before the season.

sections.title: Ownership: 75% Japanese parent, and Indian funds buying the rest

blocks.p: Sumitomo Chemical (Japan) owns exactly 75%, the most a listed company's promoter may hold, with nothing pledged. Of the 25% free float, Indian mutual funds have almost doubled their stake to 7.27% since Dec-2023 while retail holders shrank from ~149,000 to ~110,000; foreign investors own ~3.02%.

sections.title: Our forecasts: ~10% earnings growth, well below the street

blocks.p: We forecast revenue as one line, because the company reports one segment and does not give sales or profit by product. FY27 grows only ~3% after a late, deficient monsoon (Q1 domestic sales −3%); FY28-29 assume normal monsoons, new plants for the parent and steady launches (+11% and +10%). The EBITDA margin stays around 20.5-21%, at management's floor of 20%. Interest income follows the cash pile at 7.5-8.5%. Every assumption is in the Excel model's Assumptions sheet, which recalculates this report's target price.

sections.title: The street: few analysts, all BUY, all before the monsoon failed

blocks.p: Coverage is thin. Four houses have calls standing on 30-Sep-2026, all BUY: Anand Rathi ₹650 (20-Jul, a week before the Q1 results), ICICI Direct ₹625 (29-Jul, repeated 10-Aug), Elara ₹605 (April) and ICICI Securities ₹580 (May); the average is ~₹615. S&P's July poll shows nine analysts (five Strong Buy, three Buy, one Hold). None of these targets was set after the monsoon turned out deficient. The bull case rests on the parent: its molecules, its plants in India and, since July, its semiconductor-materials plans.

blocks.h: How the street values Sumitomo Chemical

blocks.p: Every broker whose method we could find values SCIL on **P/E on FY28E earnings**: ICICI Direct 45x, Anand Rathi 40x (raised from 36x for the semiconductor option), ICICI Securities 36.5x (averaged with 29x EV/EBITDA). We use the same method so that our target is comparable, applied to the earnings the market will look at in September 2027 (Sep-28E: half FY28E, half FY29E). The gap between us and the street is in the multiple and in our lower earnings, not in the method.

The DCF (₹249) is far lower: at an 11.6% cost of capital, ~20% EBITDA margins and our growth, cash flows support well under today's price. The market has always priced SCIL for faster growth than it has delivered; if growth stays at high single digits, the multiple has further to fall.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a good franchise at a price that assumes growth it is not delivering

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** one of India's widest crop-protection distribution networks, exclusive access to a global innovator's patented molecules, ~20% EBITDA margins, disciplined dealer credit and ₹2,523 cr of cash with no debt.

**What you are paying:** 33.3x our FY28E earnings for a company whose revenue has not grown in three years, whose best new idea may sit with its parent, and whose cash earns 7%, going into a deficient monsoon. On the street's method and our inputs the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): below our −5% SELL line. The cash-adjusted cross-checks are lower still.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Sumitomo Chemical India (consolidated, ₹ crore). One reportable segment (crop protection, plus environmental-health and animal-nutrition distribution). Revenue grows at a single rate; EBITDA margin is a driver; treasury income = yield × opening cash, deposits and investments. Valued on P/E, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: FY27: Q1 +1% (domestic −3% as the monsoon arrived late; exports +26%), and the June-September monsoon ended ~13% below normal, the weakest since 2015, so the kharif season will be soft; we assume H2 +6% on a normal rabi. FY28-29: a normal monsoon, new plants for the parent (Bhavnagar Q4FY27, Tarapur/Dahej FY28-29) and 1-2 launches a year. Still below the street: revenue has not grown since FY23.
assumptions._marginWhy: 20.7% in FY26; 21.9% in Q1FY27 helped by April-May price increases and low-cost opening stock. H2 is seasonally weaker (18.6% in H2FY26). Management aims to stay at or above 20%; CRISIL expects 19-20%.
assumptions._capexWhy: Maintenance ₹50-70 cr a year plus the ₹55 cr Bhavnagar plant (FY27), ₹150 cr Dahej herbicide intermediate and ₹20 cr Tarapur fitments (FY28-29), all for the parent. CRISIL: ₹150-160 cr a year over the medium term.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹66 cr ≈ 7.4% of average gross block.
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied to opening cash, deposits and investments (₹2,113 cr at Mar-26, company figure): FY26 other income ₹147 cr on ₹1,668 cr opening = 8.8%, because cash builds through the year. Q1FY27 ₹47 cr excluding the insurance claim. Lower from FY28 as deposit rates fall.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: FY27: ₹26.9 cr business-interruption insurance claim for the FY23 Bhavnagar fire (Q1FY27; Screener shows it in other income).

otherTreasury._why: Corporate deposits, bank deposits and non-current financial investments reported under other assets: the company's cash and liquid investments were ₹2,113 cr at Mar-26 vs ₹1,274 cr of cash and investments on Screener.

assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 effective 26%; new regime ~25.2% plus disallowances.

dcf._betaWhy: Debt-free with a large cash pile, but earnings swing with the monsoon: slightly below market sensitivity.
dcf._tgWhy: Indian crop-protection demand grows with farm output and prices; 6% nominal.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Industry growth of 5-6% plus share gains from the parent's new molecules.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Asset-light formulator; capex rises only for plants built for the parent.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Normal monsoons from FY28; the parent's new molecules and plants built for it lift growth to the mid-teens; Japan orders recover; margin ~21.5%.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Another weak monsoon or a glyphosate restriction; Chinese generic prices fall; growth stays in low single digits; margin ~19%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Sumitomo (ICICI Direct 45x, Anand Rathi 40x, ICICI Securities 36.5x, all on FY28E EPS). 28x = its ~42x one-year-forward median since 2023, cut by the ~23% sector de-rating (PI Industries, Dhanuka) to ~32x, and again for growth: the street's multiples come with 13-21% a year EPS growth; we forecast ~8%.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Values the business and the cash separately. A P/E on total earnings capitalises interest income at 28x, i.e. pays ~1.6 rupees for each rupee of cash. 18x ≈ the ~34x median since listing less the same de-rating and growth discount (ICICI Securities used 29x).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, Ke 11.6%, terminal growth 6%, plus net cash.
